name: The Sprouted Fronds
summary: At Denalan's garden by Lake Al'Ameth, the planted frond has taken root and sprouted. Travelers can see the new growth among the garden beds.

sections.title: A Garden by Lake Al'Ameth
sections.body: You find Denalan's garden near Lake Al'Ameth, where the botanist studies Teldrassil's peculiar plants. After a shimmering frond is planted, new fronds rise from the soil in his planter, ready to be gathered and examined.

sections.title: The Strange Flora of the World Tree
sections.body: Teldrassil is young and vast, and its plant life grows quickly. Night elf herbalists find that growth fascinating and troubling. The shimmering fronds and their offshoots show how quickly life takes hold on the World Tree's boughs, though its vitality can be hard to predict.

faq.answer: They are the plants that sprouted after Denalan planted a shimmering frond at his camp by Lake Al'Ameth. The peculiar fronds grow from it and tremble when they are ready to be gathered.
Denalan keeps his garden and research camp along the eastern edge of Lake Al'Ameth, southeast of Dolanaar in Teldrassil.

faq.q: Why does Denalan plant these fronds?
faq.answer: Denalan studies the curious, rapid growth of Teldrassil's plants. He plants seeds in prepared soil to learn about them and test for useful restorative or herbal properties.
No. These sprouted fronds are harmless plants waiting to be picked, unlike some corrupted or hostile plants elsewhere on Teldrassil's boughs.
Adventurers first find a shimmering frond in Teldrassil's wilds and bring it to Denalan. He plants it in his garden planter, hoping it will take root.
The fronds tremble as they await picking. What causes the movement is unknown.

angles.text: Denalan's research shows the practical work of gathering and studying Teldrassil's plants, and how quickly local seeds adapt to tended soil.
As a kaldorei, you help watch over and nurture the life taking root across your young World Tree.
As a druid, you can see life flourish under attentive care in Denalan's planter, even as Teldrassil faces growing perils.
